content.snl: proof(%If $F$ is continuous on $[a,b]$, differentiable on $(a,b)$, and $F(a) = F(b)$, then $F'(c) = 0$ for some $c \in (a,b)$.%, proof-step(__list__(%Since $F$ is continuous on the closed interval $[a,b]$ — which by %, %continuity on a closed interval%@BasicAnalysis.def.continuousOnIcc, % means continuity on $(a,b)$ together with right-continuity at $a$ and left-continuity at $b$ — %, %the extreme value theorem%@BasicAnalysis.thm.extremeValue, % applies, so $F$ attains a minimum at some $m \in [a,b]$ and a maximum at some $M \in [a,b]$.%)), by-cases(%The argument now splits on whether either extremum is attained in the open interval $(a,b)$.%, case(%Case 1: at least one of $m, M$ lies in the open interval $(a,b)$.%, proof-step(%Call that point $c$, so $c \in (a,b)$ and $c$ is a local extremum of $F$.%), proof-step(__list__(%$F$ is differentiable on $(a,b)$ by hypothesis, so in particular %, %the derivative%@BasicAnalysis.def.derivative, % exists at $c$.%)), proof-step(__list__(%Both hypotheses of %, %Fermat's lemma%@BasicAnalysis.thm.fermat, % are therefore met at $c$: the extremum is interior, and the derivative exists there.%)), so(%$F'(c) = 0$, and $c$ is the point the theorem asks for.%)), case(%Case 2: both $m$ and $M$ lie in $\{a, b\}$.%, proof-step(%Then the minimum and maximum values are both taken at endpoints. By hypothesis $F(a) = F(b)$, so $F(m) = F(M)$.%), proof-step(%A function whose minimum equals its maximum is constant: for every $x \in [a,b]$ we have $F(m) \leqslant F(x) \leqslant F(M) = F(m)$, forcing $F(x) = F(m)$.%), proof-step(__list__(%The difference quotient of a constant function vanishes identically, so by %, %the derivative%@BasicAnalysis.def.derivative, % every interior point has derivative $0$.%)), so(%any $c \in (a,b)$ works — and $(a,b)$ is nonempty because $a < b$.%))), proof-step(%In both cases a point $c \in (a,b)$ with $F'(c) = 0$ has been produced.%), qed)

values.en:
The proof is the two preceding theorems applied in sequence, with a case
split in between.

Continuity on the compact interval `[a, b]` yields attained extrema
(`BasicAnalysis.thm.extremeValue`). Either one of them is interior, in which
case `BasicAnalysis.thm.fermat` immediately gives a vanishing derivative there,
or both sit at the endpoints — and then the equal-endpoint hypothesis forces the
function to be constant, so every interior point qualifies.

Note where each hypothesis is consumed. Continuity is used only on the closed
interval, to obtain attainment; differentiability is used only on the open
interval, because Fermat's lemma is applied at an interior point. That asymmetry
is not an accident of this particular argument — it is what lets the theorem
apply to functions such as `x ↦ √(1 − x²)` on `[−1, 1]`, whose one-sided
derivatives at the endpoints are infinite. The hypothesis `a < b` is what makes
`(a, b)` nonempty, without which Case 2 would have no point to return.
values.zh-CN:
证明依次应用前两个定理，并在中间进行分类讨论。

闭区间 `[a, b]` 上的连续性保证极值能够取得
（`BasicAnalysis.thm.extremeValue`）。若其中一个极值点位于内部，
则 `BasicAnalysis.thm.fermat` 立即给出该点处导数为零；否则两个极值
都在端点取得，此时端点函数值相等这一假设迫使函数为常数，因而
每个内点都符合要求。

注意各项假设在何处使用。连续性只在闭区间上用于保证极值取得；
可导性只在开区间上使用，因为费马引理应用于内点。这种不对称并非
该证明的偶然现象——它使定理能够应用于函数 `x ↦ √(1 − x²)` 在
`[−1, 1]` 上的情形等例子，尽管它们在端点处的单侧导数为无穷。
假设 `a < b` 保证 `(a, b)` 非空；否则情形 2 将无点可取。
